title: Gao Kaidao
capsule: Gao Kaidao was a Chinese warlord who carved out an independent state centered on Huairong (modern Zhangjiakou, Hebei) during the chaotic Sui–Tang transition, styling himself Prince of Yan. He sustained his power through an alliance with the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, which provided cavalry support against the nascent Tang dynasty; he briefly submitted to Tang in 620 and received the surname Li before rebelling again in 621. In 624 his general Zhang Jinshu staged a coup, and Gao hanged himself; Zhang then surrendered to Tang, ending the polity.

The polity's rough geographic core is known from Tang sources, but its outer boundaries in modern Hebei and Inner Mongolia are not precisely delineated in contemporary records.
